sounds.text: The school can turn in a ring. Round and round it goes. Nobody knows why yet. In a ring, the fish swim side by side and stay in one place.

sounds.text: Whoosh! A sea lion swims up through the school. The fish move out of the way, then join up again. Sea lions eat anchovies. Most times, the fish get away.

sounds.text: Anchovies swim in a big group called a school. They all point the same way. Swimming together helps keep them safe. It helps them find food too.

sounds.text: Big animals come near. The little fish squeeze into a tight ball. In a ball, it is hard to pick out one fish.

sounds.text: Tap the water, or draw a line. The fish swim along your line and stay where it ends. Draw up to the top of the sea and they jump out! This is just for fun. Nobody has seen anchovies do it.

sounds.text: Meet the anchovy! It is a small fish, no longer than a ruler. It is blue-green on top and silver underneath, with a thin silver stripe on its side. Anchovies eat plankton. Plankton are tiny plants and animals that float in the sea. Anchovies live near the top of the sea, in big groups called schools. Lots of animals eat anchovies: bigger fish, sea birds and sea lions.
